analysis.investment_thesis: DEEPAKFERT is the most Magic Formula-friendly stock of this batch — earnings yield of ~10% (EBIT ≈ INR 1,925 Cr / EV ≈ INR 19,346 Cr) and ROCE of 15.7% make it mediocre on both metrics but reasonably balanced. At EV/EBITDA of 10.91x with a 17% EBITDA CAGR over 9 years, the price is fair but not a screaming bargain.
key_strengths: Operating income CAGR of 20.6% over 9 years with expanding EBITDA margins — the business is genuinely improving
Reasonable valuation: EV/EBITDA of 10.91x and P/S of 1.39x; earnings yield of ~10% approaches the Magic Formula 12% threshold
OCF positive all 5 of the last 5 years; FY25 OCF of INR 1,880 Cr is strong and the highest in the series
key_risks: ROCE of 15.7% is meaningfully below the 20%+ threshold I want — this is a capital-intensive chemical/fertiliser business, not a capital-light compounder
Debt load rising sharply: borrowings grew from INR 2,656 Cr (FY22) to INR 4,440 Cr (FY25) and finance costs nearly tripled to INR 413 Cr — leverage is consuming earnings
FCF was negative in FY23 and FY24 due to heavy capex (INR 885–1,209 Cr/year); CWIP of INR 2,230 Cr signals more capex ahead, making sustained FCF uncertain
red_flags: Finance cost growing at 13.7% CAGR while EBIT is volatile — debt-funded expansion compresses Magic Formula metrics if returns on new capital are modest
Net profit swung from INR 1,221 Cr (FY23) to INR 468 Cr (FY24), showing commodity-cycle sensitivity that makes 'normalized' EBIT estimates unreliable
Real estate and diversified segments add complexity and likely dilute capital returns on the core chemicals business
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EV = Market Cap INR 15,547 Cr + Debt INR 4,152 Cr – Cash INR 353 Cr = INR 19,346 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income FY25) = INR 1,925 Cr. Earnings Yield = 9.95% — just below my 12% threshold for 'attractive.' ROCE (provided) = 15.7% — below the 20% floor I prefer. The stock scores 'mediocre on both' rather than 'good on both,' which is what Magic Formula demands. That said, EV/EBITDA of 10.91x is the cheapest in this cohort and 9-year operating income CAGR of 20.6% shows real operational progress.

The structural concern is rising debt funding a large capex cycle (CWIP INR 2,230 Cr in FY25). If the new TAN (Technical Ammonium Nitrate) capacity delivers expected margins, ROCE could climb toward 18–20% and push this into buy territory. Until then, it sits in HOLD territory — reasonable but not compelling enough for the Magic Formula's systematic screen.
